title: Deployment of Tagging Technology to Alert Victims of High-risk or Violent Ex-offenders in Close Proximity
what_it_is: Deployment of Tagging Technology to Alert Victims of High-risk or Violent Ex-offenders in Close Proximity

sections.label: Alerting victims of ex-offenders
sections.summary: Minister says alerting victims to high-risk ex-offenders is not appropriate when no further crime is committed; offenders get programmes and post-release support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs whether technology such as tagging or otherwise can be adopted to alert victims of high-risk or violent ex-offenders when such offenders come within a stipulated radius or are in close proximity to them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: It is not appropriate to do so when they have not committed any further crime.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: While incarcerated, offenders who are at risk of violent re-offending are enrolled in psychology-based correctional programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Singapore Prison Service also works with the families and community partners to support ex-offenders after their release to better prevent re-offending.

sections.label: Reconciliation and family violence referrals
sections.summary: SPS refers known family violence cases to MSF and social service agencies before release, with case conferences and safety plans.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We agree with his suggestion about how we should focus on reconciliation, and that is what we hope to do for every ex-offender because that will also make their rehabilitation and reintegration process better.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: So, essentially, what we do is that for those with known family violence, the Singapore Prison Service (SPS) will refer these cases to and work with MSF and also with the relevant social service agencies before the person is being released from prison.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In some cases, we also have case conferences where we discuss deeper into the situation and see how we can help them better.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We have social service professionals, for example, those from the family violence specialist centre, who would also engage the families, not only from the reconciliation perspective, but also how to provide safety plan, in case there is re-offending.

sections.label: Taskforce on Family Violence recommendations
sections.summary: A Taskforce on Family Violence co-chaired by the Minister of State released 16 recommendations in September 2021, to be implemented over the next few years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: If you have followed the developments that we have been doing in family violence, we have formed a Taskforce on Family Violence where the Minister of State Sun Xueling and I co-chaired, and we have released a set of 16 recommendations in September 2021.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We hope to progressively implement this over the next few years.

sections.label: Protection, accountability and rehabilitation
sections.summary: Work continues to strengthen protection and support for survivors, increase perpetrators' accountability and strengthen their rehabilitation to reduce re-offending.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We are also working to strengthen protection and support for survivors to reduce their risk of being harmed again.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: And, I think, last but not least, we will increase the accountability of perpetrators and strengthen their rehabilitation to reduce their chances of re-offending.
